title: Testing Constraints and Relationships knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes “Testing Constraints and Relationships”?
options: It is a frontend styling feature and does not involve database behavior.
It guarantees correct output regardless of schema, permissions, or release version.
It is best handled by removing constraints and skipping error checks.

Schema relationships and query joins describe how rows correspond. Use keys to identify rows, foreign keys to enforce references, and normalization to reduce update anomalies; check one-to-many joins for unexpected row multiplication.
questions.answer_key: Schema relationships and query joins describe how rows correspond. Use keys to identify rows, foreign keys to enforce references, and normalization to reduce update anomalies; check one-to-many joins for unexpected row multiplication.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains: Schema relationships and query joins describe how rows correspond. Use keys to identify rows, foreign keys to enforce references, and normalization to reduce update anomalies; check one-to-many joins for unexpected row multiplication.

questions.prompt: Which practice best applies “Testing Constraints and Relationships” safely?
options: Concatenate untrusted input into SQL text and grant administrator privileges to every application user.
Judge success only by whether the statement returns any rows, without checking expected behavior or edge cases.
Join two synthetic related tables, count the result rows, and explain what happens when one side has no match.
Skip testing, assume every SQL engine behaves identically, and apply the change directly to production.
questions.answer_key: Join two synthetic related tables, count the result rows, and explain what happens when one side has no match.
questions.explanation: Join two synthetic related tables, count the result rows, and explain what happens when one side has no match. This makes the result reviewable and aligns with a controlled learning workflow.

questions.prompt: Before relying on an example for “Testing Constraints and Relationships”, what should be verified?
options: Assume a successful connection means the query and data model are correct.
Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
Run a broad production change before checking the current state.
Ignore version notes and infer behavior from an unrelated database engine.
questions.answer_key: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation.
questions.explanation: Confirm the exact MySQL version and prerequisites, predict the result, run a minimal test in a disposable environment, then inspect the evidence and relevant official documentation. The CodeLeaf editor displays reference output only; real behavior depends on the selected server/runtime.
